newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft, but anchored by GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft, but anchored by GDP data.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed softer across the board on Monday on concern over Saturday's killing of Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz's brother and sliding stock prices. But dealers said strong GDP data prevented the peso from weakening further.
"The peso slid little and the killing is not clear enough for foreigners to jump out of Mexico in force after such strong data," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.1 and 1.2 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.7730/7.7760 and 7.7700/7.7730 per dollar.
Alejandro Ortiz, brother of Finance Minister Ortiz, was shot and killed Saturday evening. Police said they were treating the crime as an attempted robbery, although no valuables were missing.
Dealers said they were uneasy as they could not rule out a political motive to the slaying.

The Finance Ministry announced early on Monday Mexico's GDP had risen 8.8 percent in year-ago terms during the second quarter, compared to an average gain of 5.92 percent expected in a prior Reuters survey.
Mexican stocks were off 29.86 points to 4,926.75 in late trade.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 2.2 centavos weaker at 7.7720/7.7740 per dollar.
